searchText: Are access list addresses and slots encoded as QUANTITY or DATA? (do we strip leading 0s before RLP encoding the byte arrays?) It *appears* they are encoded as `DATA`, which is unfortunate since that is a whole lot of wasted bytes on the wire it would seem. (most referenced storage slots will likely be low numbers) Addresses are always data > which is unfortunate since that is a whole lot of wasted bytes on the wire it would seem Wait, don't we use snappy compression on the wire already? Hmm, do we for devp2p? I don't write any devp2p code, so I don't know. Also snappy on disk? The addresses make sense as data. It is the inner array that makes less sense as data (from a compression standpoint). https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-706 Referenced storage slots will often be low numbers due to how Solidity uses them. Both rocksdb and leveldb can be configured to compress stored data. given the large amount of changes the london upgrade carries, is there a dedicated coordination chanel in case of any consensus issues?
